The Lego Star Trek: U.S.S. Enterprise Bridge diorama is a wonderful bit of nostalgia and a stunning recreation of a sci-fi icon. The playset features arguably feel a little out of place, given that the audience for this set will be older fans who want to board the Starship Nostalgia. But maybe that's the whole point: Making old Trek more accessible to young 'uns.

Beautiful diorama recreating the iconic sci-fi set.

Why you can trust Space.com Our expert reviewers spend hours testing and comparing products and services so you can choose the best for you. Find out more about how we test and review products.

It's not quite a five-year mission, but as Star Trek celebrated its 60th anniversary in September of this year (we may have mentioned it once or twice), I decided it was high time I finally watched the original Star Trek.

Before this year, I hadn't seen a single episode of "Star Trek: The Original Series", as it's now known. I'm a millennial; I grew up on "The Next Generation", "Deep Space Nine" and "Voyager". By comparison, the old series (TOS) always looked so… old and naff whenever I saw clips of it.

But now I have seen the original series. Over the course of 2026, I've ploughed through all 79 episodes, spread across three seasons. And you know what? It's pretty damn good. Even with the shiny 2006 remasters, you'll have to prepare yourself for some bad special effects work, but the scripts are interesting, the sci-fi concepts are out there, and the acting — especially from Shatner and Nimoy — is top-notch.

And just as I finally discovered a love for this classic sci-fi series, what should drop into my lap? Why it's the new Star Trek: U.S.S. Enterprise NCC-1701 Bridge diorama set from Lego. Now I have more on my wishlist to add to the Best lego space sets.

Let's start with the Band-Aid rip: this set is $200. I know; it stings, especially when Star Trek promised us a future where money doesn't exist. But at 1701 pieces (nice, I see what you did there), it's much better value from a bricks-per-dollar perspective than the X-Files set we checked out recently.

Still, that's no small investment for a toy, even if it will make a lovely display piece when it's built.

As the name suggests, you get a full Lego-ified recreation of the bridge of the USS Enterprise (NCC-1701, no A, B, C, or D). This includes Captain Kirk's chair, the helm positions ahead of him (manned by Chekov and Sulu), and all of the surrounding computer displays where you usually find Spock, Uhura and Scotty.

There's even a viewscreen that can sit in front of the crew, displaying an adorable Klingon commander facing off against Kirk.

Board the legendary starship and meet the crew of the U.S.S. Enterprise NCC-1701 for an amazing building experience. Recreate the iconic bridge and transporter room that served as the backdrop for epic scenes from "Star Trek: The Original Series".

Alongside the main bridge, there are a few fun extras bolted on, including a rotating transporter pad (which can make minifigures "disappear") and a working turbolift door connected to the back of the main bridge diorama. You'll have to make the swoosh sound effect yourself, though.

It's a wonderfully faithful recreation of Kirk's command center, complete with computer panels and screens, swiveling chairs and that weird scope thing that Spock was always looking into.

That said, it's a little lacking in proper Easter eggs. There are some tribbles hiding around the build, and the monitors have custom stickers showing cool Trekkie things. The weapon display racks on the back hold an array of pointy Klingon blades, Starfleet phasers, Sulu's fencing rapier and even Spock's harp, but compared to, say, the X-Files set we built recently, it feels a bit lacking in those deep-cut references.

All in all, it's a fantastic little diorama, but when it was announced, I'll admit I was a little puzzled as to who it was aimed at. "Star Trek fans, duh!" is the obvious response, but the Venn diagram crossover between "people who are nostalgic for the original series of Star Trek" and "people who want to buy $200 Lego sets" has to be pretty small, right?

Star Trek first aired way back in 1966, which means the first generation of fans are now 70 years old and upwards. Lord knows I hope I'm still building Lego sets when I'm 70, but is that a large enough crowd to make this set a success? Then again the show was repeated and syndicated throughout the 70s and 80s, which means hopefully there'll be some younger buyers, too.

The playset aspects of the set are even more puzzling. The working door, exploding monitor and spinning transporter pad are great additions to a kids' playset, but this isn't that — it's a display for nostalgic Star Trek fans. The design of the set just feels a bit confused.

But then it hit me. Maybe this isn't just for fans of the original series; maybe it's meant to create some new fans. I started watching the original Star Trek 60 years after its debut because… well, I'm the sci-fi editor for a space website, and it felt wrong that I hadn't seen it. But most people don't have that sort of professional impetus. The average person won't jump back to watch a 60-year-old TV show without a polite nudge, and this set does a great job of highlighting the charm and optimism of Star Trek's debut outing.

I don't know, maybe I'm just projecting here. Maybe Lego bought the rights to make Star Trek sets and needed something to do after they'd mined all the nostalgia they could from the excellent Enterprise D set they released in 2025. Maybe this is just a toy for big kids.

Or maybe… just maybe, it's meant to inspire the next generation of Star Trek fans to check out where the magic started.

Disclaimer: We were sent a copy of the Star Trek: U.S.S. Enterprise NCC-1701 Bridge set by Lego.

Ian is the Entertainment Editor at Space.com, covering movies, TV series, and games in the space and sci-fi realms. He's a massive sci-fi nerd and has been writing about games and entertainment for over eight years, with articles on sites like Space, LiveScience, GamesRadar, and more. With a degree in biology, a PhD in chemistry, and his previous role at the Institute of Physics Publishing, Ian is taking a world tour through the different scientific disciplines.

#797. How Grand Theft Auto 6 Already Raced It’s Way Into Red Carpet Fashion

With Grand Theft Auto VI already set to become the biggest game of 2026 after its Nov. 19 launch, model Alex Consani—who lent her voice to the game—showed off her GTA 6-inspired outfit.

Alex Consani is ready for a spin around Vice City.

With the supermodel lending her voice to Grand Theft Auto VI—which is poised to be the biggest video game of the year after making $3.79 billion in preorder and first-day sales, according to parent company Take Two—it was only appropriate that she channel that car vibe into her clutch look for the game’s launch party.

Consani buckled up for the Nov. 18 event at the Gekko restaurant in Miami wearing a short dress from Paris-based label Sevali’s spring 2025 collection that was made out of upcycled seatbelts. The belts crisscrossed around the 23-year-old’s svelte figure, coming to a click—literally—with a buckle that was strapped across her shoulder.

The Victoria’s Secret model completed her look with clear kitten heels and her long blonde hair parted down the middle and flowing behind her.

In the newly released video game, Consani can be heard as a DJ for the in-game radio station Flash FM alongside singer Robyn. The two play songs from the likes of Olivia Rodrigo, Charli XCX, Zara Larsson and more as they put their commentary into high gear.

After playing Rodrigo’s “good 4 u,” Consani can be heard saying in a clip posted from the game, “How do you even fumble a baddie like Olivia?”

She also had some love for Charli XCX, saying, “Whatever Charli XCX does, she’s my medicine. That is my f--king doctor, y’all.”

As for Larsson? After playing the Swedish singer’s hit “Fast Emotion,” Consani commented, “God, I love Zara so much.”

Of course, the model isn’t the only star to lend her voice to GTA VI, with Bad Bunny coming in as host of Latin radio Cocoteo FM, PinkPantheress DJing the indie dance station Stockyard FM, “Weird” Al Yankovic hosting the ’80s station Vice City FM, Morgan Wallen and Lana Del Rey co-hosting Back Country Radio and Rolling Stones guitarist Keith Richards playing his part as DJ Keith on Gloriana Blues Radio.

Grand Theft Auto VI marks the latest installment in the long-running video game series, coming out 13 years after the record-breaking Grand Theft Auto V.

The new game features characters like Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos as they take part in fan-favorite activities from previous games like car-jackings, shootouts, street-racing, robberies, swimming, jet-skiing, sky-diving, visiting the strip club and, yes, even petting dogs. GTA 6 is set around locations inspired by Floria, allowing players new playable vehicles like kayaks and airboats to roam around the new locale.

#796. Madueke 'a consistent threat' - Newcastle v Arsenal player ratings

Noni Madueke and Harvey Barnes both scored in a thrilling second half at St James' Park

Arsenal and Newcastle played out an entertaining 2-2 draw at St James' Park on Saturday.

The Gunners took the lead through Eberechi Eze in the first half before Harvey Barnes equalised after the break.

The hosts went ahead when Malick Thiaw bundled in from a corner before Noni Madueke brought the Gunners level with an excellent strike, and that is how it finished.

BBC Sport's Alex Howell has rated the players - and you can have your say too.

Lukas Hornicek: His kicking was slightly erratic. Nearly got caught on the ball by Kai Havertz after taking too long to release it. Could have done better with the second Arsenal goal. 5

Amar Dedic: Booked after pulling back Eberechi Eze and had a tough evening against the England forward. 5

Malick Thiaw: Scored the goal to put Newcastle in front, which capped an excellent performance in central defence. 8

Dan Burn: Some crucial clearances in the first half and played a big part as Newcastle took the lead. 7

Lewis Hall: A big error for the opening goal when he failed to deal with a clipped ball over the top. The left back redeemed himself with a crucial block to deny Noni Madueke and provided some excellent deliveries into the Arsenal box. 7

Sean Steur: Showed quality on the ball and a calmness you do not often see in an 18-year-old, but taken off at half time. 6

Lewis Miley: Quality on the ball and worked well with Steur. Was the deepest of the Newcastle midfield in the second half. 7

Jacob Murphy: An early shot and tried to catch David Raya off his line, but also taken off at the break after a quiet first half. 5

Joe Willock: An all-action performance and his physicality was a big reason why Newcastle improved in the second half. 7

Harvey Barnes: An excellent finish to bring Newcastle level and was always direct. 8

William Osula: Isolated as he led the Newcastle attack but did very well to assist his side's opening goal. 7

Tino Livramento (on 46, Dedic): Made a huge impact after coming on at half-time. 7

Anthony Elanga (on 46, Murphy): His pace meant Newcastle always had an option in behind. 6

Jacob Ramsey (on 46, Steur): Added drive to the midfield. 7

Subs not used: Pope, Schar, Gonzalez, Wissa, Fernandez-Pardo.

David Raya: Was taken off with what looked like a serious shoulder problem after conceding twice. 5

Jurrien Timber: Arsenal used the Dutchman's aerial ability to get up the pitch quickly. Picked up some dangerous positions when the Gunners had the ball. 6

Ezri Konsa: The centre-back looked to be cruising before Arsenal conceded twice in the second half. 6

Gabriel Magalhaes: Got caught up in a battle with Osula as Arsenal conceded a second to go behind. 6

Riccardo Calafiori: A quieter attacking display than usual from the marauding left-back. 6

Declan Rice: Started the game very well but could not stop the Newcastle turnaround. 7

Bruno Guimaraes: Had to deal with a hostile reception whenever he was on the ball. Should have scored in the first half with a great chance and then taken off. 5

Martin Odegaard: An uncharacteristic mistake to gift Newcastle a way back into the match, but then made amends by setting up Madueke. 6

Eberechi Eze: Scored the opening goal of the game with a powerful finish. Looked sharp and provided an outlet. 7

Noni Madueke: Lots of positive moments from the winger and scored a great goal to bring Arsenal level. A consistent threat. 8

Kai Havertz: Plenty of smart play and almost nicked a goal when he closed down Hornicek. Provided a great pass for Eze's goal. 7

Kepa Arrizabalaga (on 70, Raya): Made a couple of smart stops. 6

Myles Lewis-Skelly (on 70, Guimaraes): A solid performance from the bench. 7

Christos Tzolis (on 70, Eze): Worked hard after coming on. 6

Subs not used: White, Mosquera, Saliba, Hincapie.

After the opportunity to rate players has closed, the score displayed represents the average from all the submissions by BBC Sport users.

#795. Wael Mohya could make German football history at 17

At just 17, Gladbach forward Wael Mohya has earned his first Germany call-up. The dual-national talent has chosen the DFB path for now — and could soon make modern national-team history.

If you watch the Bundesliga, then you'll know Wael Mohya is a fast-footed, quick-thinking footballer. But not even the 17-year-old (Mohya turns 18 on December 31) Borussia Mönchengladbach youngster would have expected to be called up to the Germany squad so soon.

"Of course, I was absolutely thrilled. It means a great, great deal to me. I think everyone dreams of being selected for the national team at some point," Mohya said.

"And the fact that it's come to this now is, of course, just awesome and makes me very proud."

Mohya was at the gym when the call came in. He then shared the good news with his parents over dinner. "They started crying," the teenager said in a video posted on Gladbach's social media channels.

The youngster, who was born in a small town east of Düsseldorf, smiles and laughs a lot in interviews. He is always friendly, and in a good mood. On the field, too, he exudes the lightheartedness and carefree spirit of a 17-year-old.

As a technically skilled and creative player, Mohya often seeks out one-on-one situations and puts his opponents under pressure with quick dribbles. In nine Bundesliga appearances this season, Mohya has scored twice and delivered one assist.

"He's so cool and just plays really well. It's fun to watch him," Borussia coach Alexander Blessin said recently.

"Wael brings a lot to the team with his laid-back attitude on the field. He's not afraid to take risks, no matter how much pressure there is," added Gladbach's sporting director Rouven Schröder at a talk show on Sport1.

Borussia Mönchengladbach has been Mohya's sporting home since he was seven years old. Last season, previous head coach Eugen Polanski promoted him to the first team, and in December 2025, Mohya made his Bundesliga debut. Against Wolfsburg, aged 16 years and 347 days old, he became the youngest Bundesliga player in the club's history.

Mohya also recently completed a voluntary social year at an elementary school in Mönchengladbach. This is a program in Germany for young people who volunteer in the social sector — at hospitals, schools, or nursing homes, for example — for about six to 18 months. They gain work experience, help others, and earn a little money.

At the school's open all-day care program, Mohya helped serve meals, assisted children with their homework, and played with them. That's also where his nickname comes from. Because a girl hadn't understood his first name correctly or couldn't pronounce it, she called him "Waffel." Now, that name has stuck.

Even before being called up to the Germany team, clubs in the Bundesliga and across Europe's top leagues had taken notice of Mohya and were trying to sign him. His contract with Borussia Mönchengladbach runs through 2028.

With Gladbach currently in a relegation battle, his future appears likely to be elsewhere. If the club wants to generate transfer revenue from its biggest talent, next summer would likely be the opportunity to sell him — unless he extends his contract with Borussia.

The 17-year-old's career is managed by his parents. Whichever club can convince them that their son is in good hands and help him reach his full potential likely has the best chance of securing Mohya's signing.

Mohya himself says he doesn't even know how much he's currently earning at Gladbach.

"My parents take care of all that," he told Bild recently. "I get a monthly allowance, which is more than enough for me."

Germany head coach Jürgen Klopp recently revealed how much he had enjoyed his conversations with the youngster.

"The conversations I had with him were great," Klopp said with a laugh. "I wasn't that confident at 17, but then again, I wasn't that good either."

Since Mohya's parents are from Morocco, their son also holds Moroccan citizenship. As a result, he could have played for Morocco, but he has now decided against it. In fact, the Moroccan football association had been actively courting Mohya as early as last year and had already reached out to him in the run-up to the 2026 World Cup.

Now, like Frankfurt's Younes Ebnoutalib, Mohya will continue to play in the German jersey, unlike Schalke's Soufiane El-Faouzi, who chose Morocco, or Bayer Leverkusen's Ibrahim Maza, who likely would have been selected by Klopp as well if he hadn't already opted for Algeria.

For Mohya, who played for Germany's youth teams from the U16s through to the U21s, the door to Morocco remains open, even if he does play for Germany. According to FIFA regulations, players under the age of 21 can change national teams before their fourth international match (whether a competitive or friendly match), provided that none of those matches take place during a World Cup or a continental tournament such as the European Championship, Copa America, or Africa Cup of Nations.

If Mohya plays in the upcoming UEFA Nations League games in Serbia or against the Netherlands, another record is on the horizon. Although there were two even younger players who made their debuts in the Germany jersey — Willy Baumgärtner in 1908 (at 17 years and 104 days) and Marius Hiller in 1910 (at 17 years and 241 days) — the era in which they debuted is hardly comparable. And so, while Wael Mohya would rank third overall on the list, he would become the youngest Germany player in the modern era. The youngest to date was Hamburg legend Uwe Seeler in 1954, aged 17 years and 345 days.

#794. Nine wins in a row - Bournemouth & Evanilson continue to make history

Evanilson strikes again as Bournemouth see off Forest

"We have to stick together and face reality."

That is how Bournemouth manager Marco Rose responded after his side had dropped into the Premier League relegation zone with a 5-1 defeat by Chelsea.

Six weeks on, it is an entirely different story.

The Cherries are up to fourth in the top flight, having clinched a club record ninth successive win in all competitions - with five in the league.

It is a far cry from that thumping defeat at Stamford Bridge, which left Rose without a victory in his first six Premier League matches in charge.

Bournemouth earned just three points from those six games (draws against Everton, Newcastle and Brentford - when the Cherries squandered winning positions) and fans may have been fearing the worst.

From the outside looking in, it seemed as though the appointment of Rose might not deliver the fortunes that had been expected.

The 50-year-old, who accepted the unenviable task of succeeding Andoni Iraola, called for his side to take "responsibility" after the defeat by Chelsea.

"Three points after six games, we need a reaction. Everyone has to take responsibility to do better," said Rose at the time.

"We knew it was going to be a demanding season. We have to stick together and face reality. The reality is we have three points after six games."

The Cherries have not only responded to Rose's rallying cry, they have exceeded all expectations.

Those nine straight wins include five in the league - and his side are now only four points behind second-placed Brighton.

After easing to a 2-0 victory against Nottingham Forest on Saturday, Rose said: "We don't think about records, we just think about the next game.

"We took the right approach. We knew it would be tough and we would have to stay patient, and that's what we did. It was a top performance and a deserved win."

Bournemouth's nine-game winning streak is a club record - beating two separate runs of eight in 1998-99 and 2012-13

Since arriving in England in July, Rose has come across as a composed presence, regardless of Bournemouth's results.

However, the former Borussia Dortmund and RB Leipzig manager was unable to hide his delight at his side's record-breaking victory against Forest.

Shortly after the full-time whistle sounded at the Vitality Stadium, Rose unleashed a series of celebratory fist pumps in front of the delighted home fans.

It was arguably the first time Rose had let down his guard since arriving on the South Coast four months ago - and who could blame him, given the significance of the result?

It is the first time in the club's history they have won five consecutive Premier League matches.

The prospect of securing European football for a second consecutive season is growing by the week.

In addition to wins over Sunderland, Manchester United, Leeds, Ipswich and Nottingham Forest in the Premier League, Bournemouth have beaten AC Milan in the Europa League and Aston Villa in the League Cup.

Their remarkable run of nine wins across all competitions surpasses their previous record of eight, achieved in both the 1998-99 and 2012-13 seasons.

Bournemouth are currently also second in the Europa League league phase and are one of only three teams to have won all four of their matches so far.

"Tonight I will smile, but not just because of the table - because we win," Rose told Match of the Day.

Meanwhile, Justin Kluivert - who scored Bournemouth's second goal against Forest - urged his team-mates to remain "humble" and "not settle for less" before upcoming matches against Celta Vigo and Fulham.

'I'll call him' - Justin Kluivert happy he's scored same week as dad Patrick

One of the main reasons behind Bournemouth's upturn in form has been the hot streak forward Evanilson is currently enjoying.

After failing to find the back of the net in his first five appearances of the season, the Brazilian became the first player in club history to score in six consecutive Premier League matches when he broke the deadlock against Forest.

Since joining the Cherries in a club record deal from Porto in August 2024, the 27-year-old has struggled for consistency.

In his first season in England, Evanilson managed 10 goals and five assists in 31 league appearances.

Last season, though, was less productive for the forward, who managed only six goals and three assists in 36 top-flight appearances.

By scoring against Forest, Evanilson has already matched his return from the previous campaign.

"He is lovely, he works hard and his quality does the rest," said Kluivert. "I am happy he has been scoring, and working hard for the team."

It is not only goals that Evanilson is providing for his side this season. He has also proven that he is able to drop between the lines - and out wide - to allow Bournemouth to be a fluid side in transition.

That was evident for the Cherries' second goal against Forest, when Evanilson pulled out to the left touchline and threaded the ball down the line for Marcus Tavernier to cross for the unmarked Kluivert in the centre.

"The way he works for us out of possession, works as a link player and goes deep," added Rose. "The way he scores is quite impressive."

The season has not even reached the halfway point, so no-one at Bournemouth will be getting carried away just yet.

What is possible for the Cherries this term will largely depend on what happens - or, perhaps more importantly, what does not happen - in January.

Bournemouth's impressive recent form - and that of certain individuals - is likely to attract attention from some of the biggest clubs in the Premier League when the transfer window opens in January.

Players such as Evanilson, Rayan, Alex Scott and Junior Kroupi, in particular, are likely to be the subject of interest from elsewhere.

So what should Bournemouth do if some of the Premier League's 'bigger' clubs come knocking for their crown jewels?

Should they resist the premium prices the mid-season market is likely to bring and keep hold of their star quality to preserve their own aspirations this season?

Former Manchester City and England goalkeeper Joe Hart believes the Cherries should try to keep hold of their stars to bolster their own hopes this term - insisting the "sky is the limit" for Rose's side.

"Rather than setting a specific target, like Champions League qualification, they should just enjoy what they are doing," Hart told BBC Sport.

"It is crucial they keep everyone fit and firing, given they have the extra demands of playing in Europe plus the busy Christmas period to come.

"Junior Kroupi and Alex Scott came off the bench today, and that kind of squad depth could be massive for them.

"It is all about keeping themselves in the running because a lot of teams are stumbling right now, whereas Bournemouth are really in a rich vein of form."

A new supernova has been spotted exploding in the spiral galaxy NGC 1433, about 50 million light-years from Earth.

Researchers have discovered a new supernova called SN 2026ahvu. A Type Ia supernova, this event took place in a system with two stars orbiting one another (also known as a binary system), in which typically one star is an exploding white dwarf.

During most type Ia supernovae, the white dwarf pulls material away from the other star until enough accumulates on its surface to create an explosion.

Finding galaxies where stellar explosions are taking place isn't a rarity. However, this supernova is unique in how early it was captured. If the supernova were starting to dim, researchers might infer that the event was ending. However, according to details shared when it was first spotted, as well as later observations, this supernova was discovered while getting brighter.

This indicates that the supernova was likely caught early in the process of exploding, providing researchers with a unique opportunity to observe the event as it is taking place. By exploring observations of the galaxy before, during and (in the future) after the supernova event, researchers can investigate this type Ia supernova and how it affected the system in which it took place.

Scientists made this discovery using ATLAS, or the Asteroid Terrestrial-impact System, which is a robotic astronomical survey made up of telescopes across both hemispheres.

ATLAS is designed to spot incoming near-Earth objects like asteroids before they can reach Earth. It's essentially an asteroid impact early warning system.

But just because that's what the system is designed for doesn't mean that's all it can do. The system can also spot other objects moving through space and, in this instance, it was able to capture observations of this supernova.

Following its initial discovery, other observations of the supernova were made using NOIRLab's Dark Energy Camera (DECam) and Gemini South telescope.

Chelsea Gohd served as a Senior Writer for Space.com from 2018 to 2022 before returning in 2026, covering everything from climate change to planetary science and human spaceflight in both articles and on-camera in videos. With a M.S. in Biology, Chelsea has written and worked for institutions including NASA JPL, the American Museum of Natural History, Scientific American, Discover Magazine Blog, Astronomy Magazine, and Live Science. #791. 'Officials can't use common sense' - was Rogers handball correct?

Leeds dominate Chelsea for first Stamford Bridge win since 1999

It is rare when a key handball decision is given for the widespread response to be "that is correct".

Often the discussion centres on the desire for a seemingly more lenient interpretation taking into account perceived intent.

And that is again a talking point after the crucial penalty given against Chelsea in Saturday's 4-1 home defeat by Leeds which ended up putting the visitors ahead for the first time.

Interestingly, despite the perception, handball penalties are much rarer in the Premier League compared with the other top five leagues in Europe.

Last season, there were 22 penalties for handball in the English top flight's 380 games - easily the lowest tally.

Spain's La Liga (36) and Italy's Serie A (38) produced the most.

This season in the Premier League there have been three in 106 matches - less than in 2025-26.

So why was the penalty given against Chelsea's Morgan Rogers?

'Fragile' and 'miles off it' - Alonso's Chelsea honeymoon is over

Morgan Rogers turned away with his folded arms raised which led to a penalty

The feeling among Premier League clubs is that handball is in a good place now, where the arm must either be fully extended away from the body, raised, or be a deliberate act to be punishable.

And it is the last of these that applied to the penalty given against Rogers, which to some might seem a bit harsh, considering the Premier League's more relaxed interpretation of handball.

There are, however, a few key reasons why referee Michael Oliver pointed to the spot, why the video assistant referee (VAR) did not intervene, and why it will be judged as a correct decision.

Two of the factors which a referee looks for when judging a potential handball apply here.

As Jayden Bogle's shot was from distance, a defender is considered to have more time to adjust their body and react - and thus avoid a potential handball.

Most important in this case is the movement of the arm.

When Bogle shoots, Rogers' arm is not raised - but it comes up to the flight of the ball.

Crucially, had Rogers kept his arm in its original position - lower and level with his midriff - there would not have been a handball offence.

What does this mean? Put simply, if the ball would have hit the body if it had not come off the arm, it is considered to have no impact.

But this case was different. Rogers raised his arm and that is what led to the ball being deflected away. This is considered a deliberate act, and this trumps all other considerations.

'That's a terrible decision' - Onuoha critical of Rogers handball call

Perhaps there was a question about whether the ball hit Rogers too high on his arm, and thus should not be a handball offence.

It was close, but it looked like it was in what the laws call the 'red zone', the part of the arm which is punishable for handball.

But this really would be the only reason the VAR, Michael Salisbury, would have any cause to consider an on-field review.

We saw a similar case last season, in terms of how this kind of handball offence is judged - coincidentally involving a penalty awarded to Leeds.

As Anton Stach's powerful strike arrowed towards goal, Everton defender James Tarkowski leaned to his left in an attempt to block the shot - and did so with his arm, which was tucked tightly to the side of his body.

Everton manager David Moyes described the decision as "wrong", but it was absolutely correct in law.

That Tarkowski's arm was close to his side was irrelevant because of the deliberate act of leaning into the path of the ball.

Likewise, Rogers raised his arm to stop the ball and a penalty was a justifiable call.

Despite the Premier League having a more lenient interpretation of the handball law already, it is clear that many observers would like it to go further.

For example, BBC Match of the Day pundit Alan Shearer echoed many when he said there should be more intent for a handball.

"I didn't agree with the penalty when Michael Oliver gave it," he said.

"I know once the on-field decision is made there is a high bar to review it, but I don't think officials are allowed to use common sense.

"Morgan Rogers is not deliberately trying to stop the ball. He just doesn't want it hitting him in the face.

"Although the penalty came at an important point in the match, Chelsea were deservedly beaten by a much stronger, far more physical and better-organised Leeds team."

Rogers may argue he raised his arm to protect his face.

This is one of the possible mitigating factors, but usually only applies when a player raises their hands to their face - not using the arm as a barrier.

Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso said that, while he did not "want to make a big thing about it", the penalty should not have been awarded.

"For me it was quite a harsh decision," he told Sky Sports. "I would not have given a penalty. I don't want to make a big thing about it but for me it's not a penalty."

Fist my bump, everyone, because box office smash hit "Project Hail Mary" is heading back to theaters this December.

The exceptional sci-fi movie, based on Andy Weir's book, stars Ryan Gosling as Ryland Grace, a middle-school science teacher who becomes key to saving the world. Together with Rocky, an alien he meets along the way, Grace must solve the riddle of the mysterious substance that's causing the sun (and Rocky's star) to die out.

Amazon MGM has revealed the return to theaters with a video showcasing the many accolades that the film received. "Project Hail Mary" returns to the big screen on Dec. 11 and will be shown in all formats, including IMAX and 70MM.

"Project Hail Mary" was a massive success for Amazon MGM, grossing over $600 million worldwide when it first dropped in theaters back in March 2026. It was also a huge hit with critics, scoring an average of 95% on Rotten Tomatoes, and more importantly, getting two big thumbs up in our review!

Dec. 11 is a smart choice by MGM too, as it puts the sci-fi spectacle back in front of audiences a week ahead of Avengers: Doomsday and Dune: Part 3. That's not a battle you want to get in the middle of.

If you missed "Project Hail Mary" in theaters the first time, I'd definitely recommend you try to catch one of these screenings. It's a beautiful movie — visually and emotionally — and it deserves to be seen on the big screen.

If you're not feeling up to a trip to the theaters, you can also catch "Project Hail Mary" from the comfort of your own home, as it's also streaming on Amazon Prime Video.

#789. 'Fragile' and 'miles off it' - Alonso's Chelsea honeymoon is over

Leeds dominate Chelsea for first Stamford Bridge win since 1999

Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso is already in firefighting mode.

His team were booed by their own supporters at several points during a dominant 4-1 Leeds victory at Stamford Bridge, their first win there since 1999.

The first negative reaction came at half-time while the score was still 1-1. The ground then began to empty after the third and fourth Leeds goals, and the fans remaining voiced their dissent once more at the final whistle.

Although there were mitigating circumstances, including a potentially harsh penalty decision against them and the loss of midfielder Moises Caicedo to injury, joining a five-strong list of players on the treatment table, the defeat was thoroughly deserved.

It leaves Chelsea with three losses in their past four Premier League matches and they have slipped from fifth place to eighth, already 14 points behind league leaders Arsenal.

In October, Tottenham won at Stamford Bridge for only the second time in the Premier League era, while the 1-0 defeat at bottom club Sunderland before the international break was another alarm bell.

It is the first time since 1967 that Chelsea have lost at home to both Leeds and Spurs in the same season.

"We need to find solutions, for sure, because there will be setbacks during any game," Alonso said after the match.

"To be able to go through that and to know that it's still so long to play, it's something mandatory in this competition and today I felt that probably we are in a fragile moment mentally.

"When we received a punch we didn't recover that strongly."

Okafor double delivers rare win for Leeds at Chelsea

'Officials can't use common sense' - was Rogers handball correct?

Indeed, even when Chelsea have been winning matches, they have often looked unconvincing.

Yet Blues supporters chanted their new manager's name and seemed optimistic after the summer transfer business - despite a disappointing 10th-place finish last season.

Club record Â£117m signing Morgan Rogers was joined by the experienced trio of Emiliano Martinez, Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson.

It was the clinical finishing of Rogers, along with Cole Palmer and Joao Pedro earlier in the season, that masked the underlying fragility of Alonso's team.

Before this weekend, the Blues ranked 14th for expected goal difference and were joint 12th in Opta's expected points table.

After their latest setback, ex-England forward and BBC Match of the Day pundit Alan Shearer said: "Chelsea were all over the place. Once Moises Caicedo went off injured early on, there was no physicality and they looked weak.

"They hardly created anything going forward and the back four didn't look comfortable. There was no desire, cohesion or fight from the home side, but we shouldn't take anything away from Leeds.

"Two weeks ago Chelsea were bullied by Sunderland centre-forward Brian Brobbey and they let Dominic Calvert-Lewin do the same today, which is alarming.

"It's fair to say Xabi Alonso's honeymoon period is over. He needs to tell his players this simply isn't good enough. They are miles off it and have to do better in every department."

Xabi Alonso post-match interview - Chelsea v Leeds United

Xabi Alonso was appointed Chelsea manager on a four-year deal in May

In Alonso's defence, Chelsea had problems before his arrival.

They finished 10th last season, having been outrun in 37 of their 38 matches, and had three managers during a chaotic campaign.

Remarkably, Chelsea have seven more points from corresponding fixtures this season and last, but it mostly serves to show how low the bar was set.

Champions League qualification was again the club's pre-season target and Alonso's appointment was designed to bring stability and authority.

The former Real Madrid and Liverpool midfielder had an impressive playing career and earned much early admiration as a manager, guiding Bayer Leverkusen to a league and cup double in 2024.

However, the Spaniard, who was sacked by Real Madrid last season, has yet to establish any real consistency - beyond his defence leaking goals regularly.

Only Crystal Palace, Coventry City and Ipswich Town have conceded more goals than Chelsea this season.

Chelsea are also now averaging fewer than a goal per game since Joao Pedro suffered a thigh injury in training. Alongside Pedro and now Caicedo, Jorrel Hato, Maxence Lacroix, Reece James and Jamie Gittens are also injured.

It highlights how they have gained little benefit of having a season without European football.

Alonso is also beginning to face criticism from sections of the fanbase for both his team selections and substitutions.

Chief among the reasons is the constant chopping and changing of the starting XI, having now made 28 line-up changes (behind only Tottenham) while also switching between back-four and back-three systems.

In addition, Alonso is being criticised for his use of personnel, having deployed Pedro Neto as a striker on two occasions and, some would argue, not made enough use of exciting young winger Estevao.

Against Leeds he gave striker Emmanuel Emegha his first start alongside Estevao and, although the Dutch striker scored, the pair were the first players he substituted while Chelsea were chasing the game at 3-1 down.

Similarly, his late in-game interventions are under scrutiny, including the decision to bring on striker Welbeck only in the 90th minute of the defeat by Spurs.

He took until the 64th minute to make changes against Leeds when Chelsea were already 3-1 down. Only three clubs had made more substitutions in the last 15 minutes than Chelsea in the league this season.

Given Leeds' strengths, Chelsea should have been better prepared for what was coming. Before kick-off, Leeds had applied more high-intensity pressures in the opposition half than any other team in the Premier League.

They had also generated the most expected goals from set-pieces and won the most duels. Leeds maintained those trends at Stamford Bridge against a Chelsea side often accused of being soft.

Chelsea have had problems in recent seasons, but this was still their worst home defeat since a 4-1 loss to Brentford in 2022.

Likewise, it is almost uncharted territory in Alonso's managerial career, having only previously lost at home by a three-goal margin once.

The stadium emptied and supporters again left early.

Players displayed negative body language and argued with one another both during the match and after the final whistle.

As a result, Alonso has gone from needing to fix defensive issues to dealing with problems that appear to be spreading throughout the squad.

#788. 'The world got to see today' - Williams-Barnett announces himself as Spurs star

Teenager Williams-Barnett shines as Spurs beat Ipswich

Luca Williams-Barnett's performance in his first Premier League start was that good it had two of his Tottenham team-mates labelling him "incredible".

The 18-year-old winger delivered the opener with his first senior goal and then played a pivotal role in Dominic Solanke's second as Spurs comfortably beat Ipswich 2-0 at home.

As full debuts go, it does not get much better than that.

Yet what might be a sign of the excitement about his potential was manager Roberto de Zerbi calmly explaining that "his talent is bigger than this performance".

The Tottenham boss obviously believes this is just the beginning for the talented teenager.

Williams-Barnett became the youngest Spurs player to score in the Premier League since Gareth Bale against Fulham in September 2007.

They would be pretty impressive footsteps to follow in if he was to get close to the player Bale once was for the north London club.

But for the slightest of touches on his fizzed ball across the area from Ipswich goalkeeper Christian Walton before Solanke turned home, Williams-Barnett would have become the second-youngest player ever to both score and assist in a Premier League game, aged just 18 years and 51 days old.

Only Michael Owen, who did it at 17 years and 364 days for Liverpool in 1997, would have done it at a younger age.

"He's incredible, honestly," Solanke told Final Score. "We get to see him every day in training so we know what a player he is - the confidence he has, the ability he has.

"The world got to see it today, which is great for him. His confidence and ability is amazing. He'll help us a lot."

Luca Williams-Barnett scored on his first start in the Premier League

Williams-Barnett was born in Luton and played for his hometown club before moving to Spurs at the age of 10.

The teenager has been generating excitement with his performances for the club's underage teams for some time.

Back in the 2023-24 season, he played for Tottenham's Under-18s aged just 15 and in the following campaign he scored the Under-18 Premier League goal of the season against Leicester having become renowned for fine long-range strikes.

Williams-Barnett has been around Tottenham's first-team since the 2024-25 campaign as he was on the bench for three Europa League games and a Premier League match but his debut came last season as a substitute in a Carabao Cup game against Doncaster Rovers under previous boss Thomas Frank.

Last December, he scored five goals in a Under-19 UEFA Youth League game against Slavia Prague.

But this season looks to be his real breakthrough.

Williams-Barnett featured in the EFL Cup as a substitute in a 5-1 victory over Charlton in August before coming off the bench against Crystal Palace and Leeds in the Premier League.

Yet it was still a bold choice from De Zerbi to make Williams-Barnett the club's sixth youngest starter in Premier League history given Spurs were coming into this game on the back of a defeat by Leeds United which checked a recent upturn in form.

However, the Spurs boss was rewarded with a man-of-the-match worthy display.

His goal was one of endeavour as he brushed in front of Ipswich defender Abdoul Ouattara to reach Pedro Porro's cross and become the club's youngest scorer on their Premier League full debut.

Throughout the game, he was looking for the ball constantly and not afraid to run with it and try to make things happen.

"Obviously I am so happy for him, every day in the training session he shows his quality," Tottenham defender Destiny Udogie told BBC Match of the Day.

"Honestly he's just an incredible football player. I hope he keeps doing what he's doing."

The winger was unfortunate not to get the assist but the goal does not happen without his powerful cross.

The England youth international was not afraid to take on a shot and his four attempts were all on target while he had a passing accuracy of 77.4% among his 44 touches.

Only Solanke took on more shots in the game with four of his five on target.

"To see him come in and do that on his first Premier League start is crazy," added Solanke.

"He's a great person and is obviously still young, you know what young boys are like.

"But he's very dedicated and so brave on the ball which is great, in his position I think you need that."

Roberto De Zerbi post-match interview - Tottenham Hotspur v Ipswich Town

Williams-Barnett was replaced by Savio in the 64th minute which brought a standing ovation from the crowd but, with the Brazilian then being forced off later on with an injury, there may be more opportunities in the coming weeks.

Obviously there will be more excitement about the talented teenager now which De Zerbi will have to manage and he has picked midfielder James Maddison as a good mentor for the attacker.

"He's played very well, but his talent is bigger than this performance," the Spurs boss told BBC Match of the Day.

"It was the first game and I am very happy, I am very delighted for his performance, but he is a big, big, big talent.

"The management of the younger talented players is different because you can't take risks to lose their enthusiasm and their positive mentality. But I think Tottenham's dressing room now is a good environment for him.

"I put [James] Maddison to play very close to him to speak the same language but also to help him and put him in the best conditions to play. To play with freedom, to play with his qualities because his qualities are very big.

"He has to work hard but also he has to keep the passion to keep the love of football."

#787. Is AIIB's complaint mechanism failing affected communities?

The Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank has a grievance redress mechanism for people affected by projects it finances. But those seeking to file a complaint face significant hurdles. Critics say reforms are needed.

For members of the Indigenous Sasak community on the Indonesian island of Lombok, the conflict over their land is not over.

For them, a tourism and infrastructure project co-financed by the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) is a source of frustration, as they believe it has led to the expropriation of their land and destruction of their livelihoods.

In late September, they officially filed a complaint with the bank. It remains unclear whether this complaint will lead to an independent investigation.

The AIIB, which finances major infrastructure projects across Asia, has a mechanism in place to deal with such complaints.

Individuals who suffer adverse effects from the bank-financed projects may, under certain conditions, file a complaint with the institution.

However, access to this process — known as the Project Complaints Mechanism (PPM) — remains controversial.

According to a report by The Diplomat, a magazine that covers political and economic developments in Asia, none of the 45 complaints listed on the AIIB's website had been deemed admissible as of mid-September.

The bank acknowledged that "no cases have passed the PPM's eligibility assessment," but it stressed that this is "only part of the story."

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

The AIIB emphasized that not every issue needs to be resolved through this mechanism.

The PPM is "only one part of AIIB's grievance redress ecosystem," the Beijing-based bank said in response to a query from DW.

Those affected should first attempt to resolve concerns directly with the project team at the local level, it said.

According to the bank, "twelve complaints were in fact resolved at the project level — as a direct result of AIIB's follow-up and intervention — and one was resolved through domestic courts."

But critics see this as a major weakness.

"The mechanism must be easily accessible," said Arntraud Hartmann, a development economist at the Johns Hopkins University School of Advanced International Studies (SAIS Europe) in Bologna, Italy.

She argued that people affected by the projects, for instance, are required to document potential violations of environmental and social standards from the start. "How is the affected party supposed to know which standards might have been violated?" she questioned.

The AIIB disputes this claim. "In terms of accessibility, we have made the submission form simpler and translated it into 12 languages," it said, adding that complaints can be submitted online, by phone, or by email.

Urgewald, a German environmental NGO, cites another problem with AIIB-financed projects. For many of them, information on environmental impacts and resettlements is either missing or published late, it noted.

For 2024, the NGO found that 11 of the 16 projects it examined lacked complete environmental and social impact assessments. In many cases, information on the potential number of displaced residents was also missing, it added.

"The information published on the bank's website is often insufficient and inconsistent. Particularly important documents, such as environmental impact assessments or resettlement plans, vary widely or are missing entirely," said Nora Sausmikat, a China expert at Urgewald.

The lack of information makes it difficult for those affected to respond promptly and report violations early on, she underscored, adding that the situation is particularly difficult for people without formal land titles.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Christoph Steinert, a political scientist at the University of Konstanz, said the mere existence of such grievance redressal mechanisms "is not enough."

Particularly vulnerable groups often know little about their rights, he said, adding that information should be available in local languages and targeted outreach directed at affected communities.

Criticism of the AIIB's procedures is not new. A 2023 report by international aid organizations, including Recourse, Accountability Counsel, and Inclusive Development International, revealed that the AIIB's grievance mechanism had failed to accept a single complaint since its 2019 inception.

The study highlighted that 101 of the 219 AIIB-financed projects, or 46% of the total projects at the time, were ineligible for review due to co-financing exemptions.

The AIIB typically provides funding without leading projects, a standard practice in development finance. When complaints arise, it directs complainants to the lead lender. As a result, nine of the 45 complaints fell outside its jurisdiction.

For Sausmikat, this is part of the problem. "The AIIB, however, decided against revising this requirement and established a mechanism that is very difficult to access," she said.

As of January 1, 2026, following two years of external consultations, the AIIB reformed its complaints mechanism. Under certain conditions, complaints can now be filed even while legal proceedings are ongoing.

But Sausmikat stressed that the changes are insufficient. Of the eight key recommendations made by an independent expert, only three were adopted, she underlined. "The revision did not remove the actual obstacles."

The AIIB stated that the reforms are intended to make the mechanism "more accessible and responsive."

The new rules have been in effect for only 10 months, and their implementation is being closely monitored, the bank said.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Steinert said fear of reprisals poses another fundamental challenge to such procedures.

Documented cases from Latin America, for instance, show that complainants have faced administrative or legal problems, and in some cases even violence.

Such risks could deter others from filing complaints, Steinert said.  However, his research does not specifically address AIIB projects.

The bank said that it "does not tolerate retaliation against anyone who raises concerns."

"Requestors may ask for confidentiality, and the revised PPM policy strengthens protection against reprisals," it added.

Sausmikat said Germany — as a co-founder and the fourth-largest shareholder of the AIIB — could also play a role, working with other member states to push for changes.

Hartmann also stressed that the bank's shareholders bear responsibility and urged the AIIB's Board of Directors to amend the rules governing the grievance mechanism. "We need a policy based on good-practice standards."

#786. 'A shotgun marriage': Why are NASA's SkyFall Mars helicopters riding on a nuclear rocket?

"The connection to Space Reactor-1 seems to me to be a bit of a shotgun marriage, a tech-demo piggybacking on another mission as an opening bid for a 'nuclear NASA.'"

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The pace is picking up on building, testing, and plotting out the flight paths for a trio of NASA Ingenuity-class helicopters to investigate Mars after riding there on a nuclear-powered rocket.

NASA's Skyfall mission will see those mini-choppers dropped off at Mars by the space agency's Space Reactor-1 Freedom (SR-1) rocket, the first fission nuclear-powered interplanetary spacecraft slated for launch in late 2028. After its cruise phase and initial Mars flyby in 2029, that nuclear carrier craft will make a second Mars approach in the Fall of 2030 to unleash a SkyFall entry capsule outfitted with a fleet of small aerial vehicles that will soar across the Red Planet.

But some experts are questioning why NASA is combining two such high-profile missions into one. "It is clear that SkyFall was approved for programmatic or political reasons," said Scott Hubbard, former director of NASA's Ames Research Center and the first Mars Program Director (aka the "Mars Czar") at NASA Headquarters, told Space.com. "The connection to Space Reactor-1 seems to me to be a bit of a shotgun marriage, a tech-demo piggybacking on another mission as an opening bid for a 'nuclear NASA.'"

Hubbard is a retired adjunct professor of aeronautics and astronautics at Stanford University. He is a major voice in shaping Red Planet exploration goals, drawing upon his expertise as NASA's former foremost Mars authority. His understanding is that the basic concept had been developed as a follow on to Ingenuity, an attempt to move beyond a technology demo and into a science platform.

Hubbard said that combining these two observations, the outcome presents "an unusual set of management issues." Since the SkyFall mission concept first appeared, he said, the usual sequence for a science mission is reversed.

"The science community is having to scramble to back into a set of requirements and objectives that match the SkyFall capabilities. Fortunately the community is very creative," said Hubbard, "and the basic Planetary Decadal objectives are very broad."

Decadal surveys reflect a broad consensus within the scientific community and provide detailed insights into the strategic priorities and mission directives set for the next decade across key scientific domains, including planetary exploration.

However, Hubbard said he has heard griping about the "fait accompli" process, "but the planetary community will make lemonade."

It should be noted however, Hubbard continued, that this process is not how you would design a strategic set of missions as precursors for human exploration.

"SR-1 Freedom is a technology demo that may or may not be ready for the Mars launch window in 2028. It is clear that the Mars Program has a standard launch concept in their back pocket," said Hubbard. "Nuclear Electric Propulsion [NEP] is of little value in traveling to Mars, not shaving any time off the transit. The real value of NEP is for risk reduction, use at the moon, outer planets and even bolder ideas like interstellar travel," Hubbard concluded.

"This, by far, is the shortest Mars mission ever conceived of," said Matthew Golombek, SkyFall Project Scientist at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Pasadena, Calif., speaking Nov. 10 during the virtual meeting of the Mars Exploration Program Analysis Group (MEPAG).

Kick-started by NASA in March 2026, the SkyFall project has grown from roughly six people to over 200 individuals who are now working on the initiative, said Golombek. "This is an incredibly rapid development and build," he said.

"It's really to demonstrate that exploration is possible with helicopters … filling what I call a 'resolution gap' between orbital information and surface information," Golombek told the MEPAG.

Once deployed by a helicopter deployment system, the threesome will spin up their rotors at about a kilometer above the surface of Mars. Then each helicopter lands on its own, ready to undertake flights every other solar day on the Red Planet. On average, a day (labeled as a sol) on Mars lasts 24 hours 39 minutes 35 seconds, from one noon to the next.

SkyFall's prime mission is six months, with a one-year goal," Golombek said, and the intent is to arrive in northern spring on Mars, a time where the vehicles are unlikely to encounter dust storms.

On the to-do list of NASA level one science requisites are for the helicopters to capture high-resolution imagery, perform a set scientific tasks, and help to prepare for future human exploration of Mars, said Golombek.

From their initial landing spots, the whirlybirds could potentially go tens to 100's of kilometers or more in different directions. Identical for all three helicopters, the nominal payload consists of five instruments, plus engineering navigation cameras.

That gear can examine the subsurface structure of Mars, the geomorphology and geology of surface terrains, as well as look at the meteorology of the atmosphere and the planet's radiation environment.

"The real star of the show is ground penetrating radar [GPR] with a flexible antenna," Golombek noted. That ultra-small GPR hardware can look for buried rocks, the layering of the Mars home turf, as well as spot subsurface ice deposits.

"If you have this aerial access and the ability to scout ahead," Golombek said, "you would go a long way towards better defining where to go with a rover and what kind of more detailed surface studies to do with subsequent missions."

All that said, yet to be plotted out are science-focused traverses for the SkyFall helicopters. But there are early ideas.

"The real kicker is that these spacecraft are the smallest landers ever attempted on Mars," said Golombek. "You are looking for a place that virtually has no rocks," he pointed out, a must-have to assure high probability of landing safely. So toss in for good measure low surface slopes, no big craters, a site not overloaded with dust.

One early idea is to revisit the crash locales of discarded SkyFall descent hardware – fuel tanks, cruise stage and associated gear – equipment large and heavy enough to survive entry, smack into the Mars landscape and high-speed and generate craters.

"So if there is ice at centimeters depth, we would create our own icy impact craters," Golombek said. "We could actually visit them in a time-scale before the ice actually sublimates," he said.

Another site getting the eye, albeit deemed a design reference target but considered a "pretty good spot," is within Arcadia Planitia in Mars's northern lowlands. Studies have indicated the presence of substantial volumes of near-surface excess ice there.

"There is a vast amount of information to suggest large quantities of regional ice deposits at that location," said Golombek. "This is at least one location that appears to meet all the engineering constraints and would be a potentially safe landing site…virtually no rocks," he advised.

In the past, Golombek added, JPL took part in SpaceX-sponsored workshops to look for ice deposits as close to the equator of Mars that could be found. Arcadia Planitia was flagged as superior Starship touchdown terrain.

"Most of the landing sites considered for humans have talked about going to places with ice deposits. Ice provides both a consumable as well as fuel to get back off the planet," said Golombek.

For the near-term, scientific community input next year — via two workshops — are on tap, reviewing the science of SkyFall and also help sort out potential landing sites for final decision-making at NASA Headquarters.

Meanwhile, as SkyFall literally spins up, there is the need for on-time delivery of Space Reactor-1 Freedom.

Golombek said NASA considers the two endeavors as a pair.

"If SR-1 is not ready, SkyFall could be launched on any conventional launch vehicle without any difficulty whatsoever," said Golombek, "something like a Falcon 9 would be more than sufficient, but others are possible as well."

Leonard David is an award-winning space journalist who has been reporting on space activities for more than 50 years. Currently writing as Space.com's Space Insider Columnist among his other projects, Leonard has authored numerous books on space exploration, Mars missions and more, with his latest being "Moon Rush: The New Space Race" published in 2019 by National Geographic. He also wrote "Mars: Our Future on the Red Planet" released in 2016 by National Geographic. Leonard  has served as a correspondent for SpaceNews, Scientific American and Aerospace America for the AIAA. #785. Beverly Hills, 90210 Alum Kimmarie Johnson’s Cause of Death Revealed

Kimmarie Johnson, who appeared on Beverly Hills, 90210 in 1998, died as a result of cardiopulmonary arrest, with ovarian cancer as an underlying cause, per her death certificate.

Authorities have determined what led to Kimmarie Johnson’s death.

Two weeks after the actress, who appeared in Beverly Hills, 90210 and Dude, Where’s My Car?, died Nov. 3 following what her niece described as a “heart event,” her cause of death was determined to be cardiopulmonary arrest, according to a death certificate obtained by People, who listed her age as 59.

While a heart attack—medically referred to as myocardial infarction—is the result of a blocked artery, cardiopulmonary arrest—or cardiac arrest—is when the heart stops beating and is unable to effectively pump blood to the body, according to the Cleveland Clinic.

Johnson’s death certificate also listed an underlying cause as metastatic granulosa cell ovarian tumor with peritoneal carcinomatosis, meaning the rare type of ovarian cancer she had spread to her abdominal area, according to the Mayo Clinic.

After her death, Johnson’s niece Rhonda Scott reflected on the joy her aunt brought into the world.

“She radiated a light so strong and bright,” Scott told People in an interview published Nov. 5. “People who came in contact with her felt nothing but positive energy. We will miss her tremendously and will continue to honor her life forever.”

Johnson graduated from Wilkinsburg High School in Pittsburgh in 1985 before studying at California University in Pennsylvania. She won the title of Miss Pennsylvania USA in 1993 and was subsequently a finalist at the Miss USA pageant.

She later moved to New York City and then Los Angeles, where she pursued a career in modeling. While Johnson found small roles on the big screen over the years, she launched her skincare brand SkinGlow by Kimmarie in 2011 and continued to model until her death.

She is survived by her son Cameron Nino, with whom she shared a special connection.

“My [son], u are bright, honest, kind, intelligent, funny and compassionate,” Johnson wrote on Facebook last November alongside a picture of her son for his 22nd birthday. “I’m glad that you enjoyed a good day.”

#784. Mathematicians astounded by AI and human-written proofs of iconic Riemann hypothesis

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

The Riemann hypothesis has been a lodestar for generations of mathetmaticians. Credit: James Brittain/Getty

In a year that has seen artificial intelligence reach one spectacular mathematical breakthrough after another, Anthropic has now claimed the top prize of them all: a full proof of the Riemann hypothesis, the statement that many mathematicians consider the most important open problem in the field. But on the same day as the Anthropic claim, a separate study claiming to have proven the Riemann also emerged — and this one is entirely human written.

The Anthropic announcement came on 20 November from Levent Alpöge, a mathematician at the San Francisco, California company. “I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis,” Alpöge wrote, referring to Anthropic’s large language model (LLM).

“If this fully checks out, it is clearly a historic milestone in mathematics,” says number theorist James Maynard, a Fields Medal winner at the University of Oxford, UK, says.

Anthropic AI ‘formalizes’ proof of Fermat’s last theorem — a milestone for mathematics

Anthropic AI ‘formalizes’ proof of Fermat’s last theorem — a milestone for mathematics

Hours later, Ravi Vakil, a mathematician at Stanford University in California, posted online a rival preprint to Alpöge’s, in what Vakil called a “hurried announcement.” The preprint was written by Alessandro Maria Masullo, a mathematician who received his PhD at Stanford in 2020 under the supervision of number theorist Brian Conrad. “The hope was to have Brian work with Alessandro for a year to polish the writing and then announce it after running it by enough people,” Vakil wrote. “Now it seems best to put out the current draft.”

The confirmation of either or both solutions would be a spectacular bicentenary present for Bernhard Riemann, the German mathematician who was born 200 years ago this September and who formulated the problem, which addresses the distribution of prime numbers, in the mid-1800.

The Riemann hypothesis is one of the seven Millennium Prize Problems selected by the Clay Mathematics Institute, which has its scientific headquarters in Oxford, UK , at the turn of the twenty-first century. The institute offers a US$1 million prize to anyone who devises a solution to one of the problems, which are considered some of the most challenging in the field. Mathematicians using AI tools announced earlier this year that they had solved another Millennium problem, related to the Navier-Stokes equation.

The problem has to do with the ‘Riemann ζ function’ (ζ is the Greek letter zeta), which encodes the randomness properties of the prime numbers. Riemann discovered that the distribution of primes is encoded in the ζ function’s ‘zeroes.’ These are points, denoted by z, on a plane satisfying the equation ζ(z) = 0.

Riemann conjectured that apart from some obvious but uninteresting cases, all such solutions had to lie on a certain vertical line in the plane. If this were true, he showed, it would imply that prime numbers are scattered among all whole numbers in a way that is essentially as random as it could be.

Alpöge’s 4-page document includes a sketch of the proof. But Andrew Granville, a number theorist at the University of Montreal in Canada, says that Alpöge should have taken the time to prepare a clearer write-up before making the announcement, which came just days after Anthropic’s initial public offering (IPO). The IPO initially valued the company at US$1.5 trillion, but the company’s valuation dropped on 19 November.

“What he released is garbled,” Granville says of Alpöge’s document. Granville cites the downturn in the company’s stock value as the reason for the timing of the proof’s release.

“There is an obvious cynical view, to do with the timing, but it is false,” Alpöge wrote in the document.

Anthropic did not respond immediately to Nature’s request for comment.

Tristan Buckmaster, a mathematician at New York University who collaborated with Alpöge on a separate project regarding the Navier-Stokes equation, says that Alpöge deserves a lot of credit for developing techniques to produce mathematical results using LLMs. “Levent himself built this amazing setup to do math”. He adds that Alpöge, who is himself a number theorist on leave from Harvard University in Cambridge, Massachusetts, has been working relentlessly for months on this and other problems, hardly ever getting any sleep.

‘The job description is changing’: mathematician Terence Tao on the rise of AI

‘The job description is changing’: mathematician Terence Tao on the rise of AI

“I suspect that the proof will turn out to be correct,” Maynard says of the Alpöge announcement, even though it is now in the form of incomprehensible code in the Lean programming language.

“At the moment, it apparently is crazily complicated. It’s going to take a long time for mathematicians to digest,” says Buckmaster. Maynard agrees, but he adds, “assuming we do get the corresponding understanding, this will surely be viewed as one of the absolute pinnacles of mathematical results”.

#783. Raya set to have scan on injury - how much would Arsenal miss him?

David Raya has made 163 appearances since joining Arsenal in 2023

Injuries are never good news, but Arsenal's latest one to first-choice goalkeeper David Raya has come in the worst possible position.

The 31-year-old was forced to leave the pitch 70 minutes into Saturday's 2-2 draw with Newcastle, appearing to hurt his shoulder in an innocuous challenge with Magpies forward William Osula.

The Gunners arguably have the best depth in the league with at least two quality options in all outfield positions after a period of squad strengthening.

In goal, however, cover appears much thinner.

Raya was a key component in Arsenal's Premier League title-winning campaign last season, was named in the Fifpro Men's World 11 and was unlucky to not win the Yashin Trophy, awarded to the world's best goalkeeper, which went to Spain team-mate Unai Simon.

Behind him, Kepa Arrizabalaga still holds the record as the most expensive goalkeeper in football history following his Â£72m move from Athletic Bilbao to Chelsea in August 2018, but is far behind Raya in terms of quality.

Raya's passing range and ability on the ball are key to how Arsenal build their attacks, and his presence is a big reason why they have the best defence in the league.

They have conceded just seven Premier League goals this season, with only Brighton able to match that tally - having played a game fewer.

Arsenal also brought in former Leeds goalkeeper Illan Meslier on a free transfer in the summer but his only appearance this season came in the embarrassing Carabao Cup defeat by League Two Fleetwood.

When asked about Raya's injury, Arteta said he did not know how severe the issue is.

"Well, unfortunately, he had to come off, which is never good news," said Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta.

"He will get assessed now, and probably he will have an MRI [scan] tomorrow to see what it is exactly he has done.

"I don't know how it happened, and what the injury is at the moment, so we'll have to wait and see tomorrow."

Who was 'a consistent threat'? Newcastle v Arsenal player ratings

Arsenal go six clear after lively draw at Newcastle

Arsenal are about to enter a gruelling period of games - with or without Raya.

In the next four weeks, they face Borussia Dortmund, Manchester City, Brentford, Tottenham Hotspur and Real Madrid.

"The one player that Arsenal cannot afford to lose is David Raya," said former England forward Alan Shearer, who is a pundit on Saturday's BBC Match of the Day. "He has made such a difference since joining from Brentford in 2023.

"They have top-class cover in just about every other position but he is the one individual that Mikel Arteta will be thinking 'we don't want to play without him for an extended period'. They could, of course go into the transfer market if they need to in January, but Arteta will be desperately hoping Raya is not out for long."

Raya is reportedly close to agreeing a new deal at the club, which shows his importance to the Gunners with two years remaining on his contract.

Ex-England midfielder Jamie Redknapp said on Sky Sports that Raya is "irreplaceable".

"Kepa is not up to the level of him - I actually think he struggles in the Premier League," added Redknapp. "Obviously we've seen in the Carabao Cup last year in the final.

"He is now going to have to play some games and that's going to be difficult for him.

"It will change everything for Arsenal for a while so that's a massive blow depending on how long David Raya is out because he is irreplaceable - probably the best goalkeeper in the Premier League, if not one of the best in the world."

#781. Nicole Richie Reveals Daughter Kate Has “Surpassed” Her in This Way

Nicole Richie shared that when it comes to the world of beauty, her and husband Joel Madden's 18-year-old daughter Harlow Kate Madden has completely eclipsed her mom.

Nicole Richie has a simple solution for her beauty needs.

The Simple Life alum revealed that her and husband Joel Madden’s 18-year-old daughter Harlow Kate Madden has become her go-to makeup artist, as the teen is even more skilled than she is in that particular area.

“I would say that she has surpassed me,” Richie told People in an interview published Nov. 19. “She’s so good. I actually am not very good at doing my own makeup. She is a whole different animal.”

And the 45-year-old knows exactly how her daughter—who chooses to go by her middle name Kate—got so good at glowing up her family.

“She grew up watching YouTube tutorials,” Richie explained, “and she’s so well-versed in makeup and contour and highlighting and just all the things.”

“If I ever need my makeup done at home, I’m going to her,” the House of Harlow founder added. “It’s not me doing it ... She kills a cat-eye.”

Of course, Kate will soon be showing off more of her talents as she officially builds the foundation for a modeling career after signing with The Lions Management.

“I’ve always dreamed of modeling, so getting to start this next chapter with The Lions is incredibly exciting,” Kate shared in a Nov. 20 statement to Women’s Wear Daily. “Fashion has always been a way for me to express myself, and I can’t wait to explore that in a whole new way.”

She added, “I’m looking forward to learning, growing, meeting new people, and seeing where this journey takes me.”

Kate made her modeling debut alongside her mom for Balenciaga’s recent campaign celebrating the 25th anniversary of their Le City handbag, a style Richie was particularly fond of in the early 2000s.

And Madden—who also shares son Sparrow James Midnight, 17, with Richie—was particularly thrilled to see his daughter achieving her dream.

The Good Charlotte frontman reposted Kate’s modeling announcement to his Instagram Stories Nov. 20, captioning it with three red heart emojis and writing in all caps, “KATE!”

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

United Launch Alliance (ULA) is getting a handle on why its Vulcan Centaur rocket failed over the weekend.

That failure, which occurred during a launch from Florida's Space Coast on Sunday (Nov. 15), led to the loss of 40 Amazon Leo internet satellites. ULA soon traced the anomaly to Vulcan Centaur's first stage, and it has now pinpointed the problem area even further.

"While work remains to determine cause, preliminary indications are that the low booster thrust was the result of inadequate fuel supply from the vehicle to the BE-4 engines, not from the performance of the engines," ULA wrote in an update today (Nov. 18).

This is good news for Blue Origin, Jeff Bezos' aerospace company, which builds the BE-4. Two of these engines power Vulcan's first-stage booster, and they're also key to Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket: That heavy lifter features seven or nine BE-4s in its first stage, depending on the configuration. (New Glenn has its own issues at the moment; it exploded during a test on May 28, and Blue Origin is working to return the powerful rocket to flight.)

ULA had already said that Vulcan's six solid rocket boosters (SRBs) and its Centaur V upper stage — which employs a different engine, the RL-10 — seem to perform well on Sunday. Further analysis is firming up that conclusion, according to today's update.

Vulcan has had issues with its SRBs in the past. On the rocket's second and fourth flights — which launched in October 2024 and February of this year, respectively — an SRB nozzle burned through and fell off about 30 seconds into flight. On both occasions, Vulcan overcame the problem and successfully delivered its payload to orbit.

In the wake of the February flight, ULA and Northrop Grumman, which builds the SRBs, tweaked the nozzle design — a fix that apparently worked, based on Sunday's nominal performance.

Sunday's launch was the fifth ever for the two-stage Vulcan Centaur, the successor to ULA's workhorse Atlas V rocket. Vulcan debuted in January 2024 and has now experienced issues on three of its five flights, though Sunday's was the only one that ended in failure.

Vulcan was out of action for about nine months after the February SRB issue. It's unclear how long its current grounding will last; that depends on what ULA's anomaly investigation, which the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration is overseeing, ends up finding.

Michael Wall is the Spaceflight and Tech Editor for Space.com and joined the team in 2010. He primarily covers human and robotic spaceflight, military space, and exoplanets, but has been known to dabble in the space art beat. His book about the search for alien life, "Out There," was published on Nov. 13, 2018. Before becoming a science writer, Michael worked as a herpetologist and wildlife biologist. He has a Ph.D. in evolutionary biology from the University of Sydney, Australia, a bachelor's degree from the University of Arizona, and a graduate certificate in science writing from the University of California, Santa Cruz.
